findings.title: findMany method removed, breaking callers
findings.body: The service previously exposed a `findMany` method used by consumers of InsightsBookingService to query bookings via Prisma's typed API. This PR removes `findMany` entirely and only exposes `getBaseConditions`, which returns a raw `Prisma.Sql` fragment that callers must manually interpolate into `$queryRaw`. Any existing caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` (e.g. API routes or other services) will now fail to compile/run. The PR description and diff do not show any check or migration of callers of this now-removed method, which is a breaking API change not reflected in the integration tests update.

findings.title: Caching tests removed without replacement
findings.body: The previous test suite included a 'Caching' describe block verifying that getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions results are cached across calls. This block was deleted entirely in the PR, removing coverage of the caching behavior (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions) that still exists in the service implementation. No equivalent test was added to validate caching still works correctly with the new Prisma.sql return type.

findings.title: Potential SQL fragment growth with large ID lists via ANY(array)
findings.body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition now use `ANY(${ids})` with parameter arrays passed directly into Prisma.sql. For orgs/teams with very large membership, this creates a single large array parameter; while likely fine, it changes from Prisma's `in` operator semantics to raw SQL ANY, and should be verified for correct parameter binding/escaping especially given these ids come from DB-generated integers (likely safe) but any assumption on this being type-checked by Prisma is weakened since this is now a raw SQL path.
